articles.title: Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as traffic exhaust, study suggests
articles.summary:
Research finds highest levels of cancer-related PAH pollutants in cities that have widespread wood heating

Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to…

blocks.text: Children’s exposure to home wood-burning could be as significant as exposure to traffic exhaust, suggests new research across six European towns and cities.

Scientists measured the air in buildings where children spend much of their time; in schools, sports centres and homes. Specifically, they looked at polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH), a family of pollutants that are given off when fuels are burned.

Dr Barend van Drooge, from Barcelona’s Institute for Environmental Assessment and Water Research (IEAWR) and senior author of the study, said: “Some of these compounds are related to cancers after prolonged exposures, as recognised by the International Agency for Cancer Research, and evidence exists that they delay cognitive development.”
Measurements were made in and around Athens, Barcelona, Colchester, Copenhagen, Helsinki and Lisbon.
Van Drooge continued: “Urban areas with wood-burning, such as Colchester and Athens, had the highest PAHs levels. Barcelona and Lisbon, where wood-burning is not practised, had the lowest levels.”
In Colchester and Athens, PAH exposure was greater than the World Health Organization guidelines.

Maria Antonia Aretaki, of the IEAWR in Barcelona and first author of the study, said: “Understanding the pollutants in children’s everyday surroundings is an important step towards protecting their health. Children are particularly important given their vulnerability to environmental pollutants and the potential health implications from exposure during childhood.”

Sports centres had the lowest concentrations. This was followed by schools, through some, especially those in Lisbon, were affected by nearby busy roads. Ventilation and indoor sources were important, but the homes with some of the greatest PAH were in areas with wood-burning, and many had open fireplaces and stoves.
Winter PAH concentrations were greater than summer.

The researchers divided the PAH into two types, according to molecular weight. In the Colchester homes, the high-molecular-weight PAH in winter were more than 10 times those in summer. The low-molecular-weight PAH were around three times greater.

Van Drooge continued: “Wood-burning is known to be an important emitter of PAH, but it was surprising that it has become such an important contributor to the overall presence of PAHs in urban areas. However, none of the cities exceeded unacceptable limits for lifetime cancer risk.”

Within the UK, the impacts of wood-burning are unlikely to unique to Colchester. Separate analysis of energy performance certificates by researchers at University College London showed that Colchester ranked 120th out of 333 local councils for density of wood burners per square kilometre. Worthing, Norwich and Reading all had around four times more.

A wintertime study of 53 children from two primary schools in Anglesey (Ynys Môn) found that children living in homes with wood burners could be exposed to over three times more particle pollution than those in non-wood-burning homes. The Anglesey study also found that homes had more air pollution than schools.

In Greece, wood-burning increased during the financial crisis that began in 2008. The cost of heating oil soared and many people turned to wood heating. This contributed to increased deaths associated with particle pollution in Athens, especially for those aged over 70. In some Greek towns, wood-burning leads to PAH that are 100 times greater in winter compared with summer.

articles.title: Boxer on death row in Iran vows ‘not to bow before oppression’ after winning rights prize
articles.summary:
Political prisoner Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran, given prestigious Magnitsky humanitarian award

A boxer and political prisoner on death row…

blocks.text: A boxer and political prisoner on death row in Iran said he will “never surrender” as he accepted a prestigious human rights prize on behalf of “the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives”.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, an Iranian boxing champion, coach and political prisoner, has been sentenced to death three times and is one of seven athletes at risk of execution in Iran. He was given the Magnitsky award for outstanding human rights activist at a ceremony in London on Thursday night.

In a written message from Vakilabad prison in north-eastern Iran, he said: “I accept this award in the name of all those who, for the ‘crime’ of aspiring to a free Iran, have been imprisoned, tortured, threatened, or sentenced to death; in the name of my comrades in the resistance units and the generation that is paying the price of freedom with their lives.”
He added: “The regime demands repentance, televised confessions and surrender from us. But our answer is clear: ‘We will never surrender; we will never submit to humiliation.’”

blocks.caption: Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani: ‘We will never surrender; we will never submit to humiliation.’ Photograph: Iran Human Rights

blocks.text: Vafaei Sani, 31, was arrested in 2020 for taking part in nationwide democracy protests in 2019 and accused of supporting an opposition group, the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK).

He was convicted of “corruption on Earth” and sentenced to death for a third time in September 2024 after “a grossly unfair trial”, according to Amnesty International. The supreme court upheld his death sentence on 4 October 2025. Since his arrest he has been tortured and held in solitary confinement for extended periods.

His continued imprisonment has drawn widespread international condemnation from prominent sportspeople, human rights organisations and legal experts who have called for his immediate release and the annulment of his death sentence.

The Magnitsky awards are named after the Russian lawyer, Sergei Magnitsky, who died in Russian police custody after exposing government corruption. They began in 2015 as a way to recognise journalists, politicians and activists in the field of human rights.

Sir William Browder, head of the Magnitsky Justice Foundation and the chair of the awards committee, said Vafaei Sani’s case was emblematic of the plight of many Iranians who face execution for standing against the regime. “Most important, Mohammad Javad is still alive,” he said. “That is why this award matters. Every time the world pays attention, it becomes harder to kill him quietly.”

blocks.caption: The awards are named after lawyer Sergei Magnitsky, who died in Russian police custody. Photograph: Alexander Zemlianichenko/AP

blocks.text: According to the Hengaw Organisation for Human Rights, at least 710 people have been executed in Iran since the beginning of 2026, including 79 political and religious prisoners.

In an October report, the organisation documented at least 106 death sentences against January protest detainees, 35 of whom had already been executed. In Vakilabad prison, where Vafaei Sani is detained, five people have been executed linked to the protests and 15 others are facing death sentences.

Vafaei Sani’s award comes at a time when there are growing fears for imprisoned Iranian athletes, who are considered role models in the country. Zohreh Abdollahkhani, founder of Human Rights for Sport, said: “The situation is really dire … We have seven athletes at risk of execution now, including Vafaei Sani.”

Ali-Sina Mostafavi, a mountaineer, was executed on 14 October after the anti-government protests. His death followed the killing of Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi, a taekwondo athlete, earlier that month, and the mixed martial arts fighter Gholamreza Khani Shakarab, who was hanged in May.

Abdollahkhani said people had been celebrating Vafaei Sani’s award. “Even people who don’t support his political view are supporting him to be heard,” she said. “I find it very inspiring that different political groups are coming together to say no to execution.”

In his message, Vafaei Sani said he wanted “a free and democratic Iran … where the people vote freely, women and men are equal, there is no discrimination on the basis of ethnicity, religion or belief, and no one is imprisoned or executed for political opposition”.
He added: “I remain steadfast in my pledge, and I will not bow before oppression until the people of Iran are free.”

articles.title: Students stage walkout vs. Trump visit, Pax Silica: 'We fight for our future'
articles.summary: Student groups from different universities staged campus walkouts on Friday to protest the upcoming visit of US President Donald Trump for the ASEAN 2026 Summit and the America-led Pax Silica…

blocks.text: Published November 13, 2026 1:58pm

Student groups from different universities staged campus walkouts on Friday to protest the upcoming visit of US President Donald Trump for the ASEAN 2026 Summit and the America-led Pax Silica initiative.
At the University of the Philippines (UP) Diliman, students staged a campus walkout and rally to voice their indignation during what is called the National Youth Day of Action.

In a video report by Ian Cruz from UP Diliman, Kabataan Partylist Representative Renee Co called Trump a "rapist, pedophile, warmonger" who used the world's resources to pursue war for the benefit of his friends and artificial intelligence industries. She also slammed alleged plans to set up AI data centers into the Philippines.

"We don't want to sell the future of the youth. That's why behind me are the Gen Z of the Philippines, who stand in solidarity with the Gen Z of the world. We fight for our future and Donald Trump is not a part of this picture," Co said in a mix of English and Filipino.

In Ateneo de Manila University, students and university personnel also staged a walkout, according to student publication The GUIDON. Many protesters were seen carrying signs to reject the Pax Silica initiative and to protect the environment.

Students from the Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP) also held a mass walkout. Bayan Muna Partylist shared that their student chapter had joined the national protest action to reject Trump and Pax Silica.

"Mariing tinutulan ng mga kabataan ang Pax Silica na may kaugnayan sa estratehiya ng US sa critical minerals at semiconductor supply chains. Nananawagan ang Iskolar ng Bayan ilantad sa publiko ang buong nilalaman ng kasunduan at tiyaking mapangangalagaan ang pambansang interes," Bayan Muna said in Facebook post.

(The youth strongly reject Pax Silica, which is connected to the US' strategy regarding critical minerals and semiconductor supply chains. The Scholars of the Nation are calling for transparency to the public on the full contents of the agreement and to ensure national interests.)
Several other student groups have announced protest activities later in the day and in the days leading up to the ASEAN Summit.
The Pax Silica initiative, which is set for construction in New Clark City in Tarlac, has been the subject of controversy for several months.

Multi-sectoral groups have raised concerns over its possible impact to the environment due to its high energy and water consumption, and the potential displacement of indigenous people from their ancestral lands.

Earlier this week, the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) reiterated that Pax Silica in New Clark City will be governed by Philippine laws. The BCDA also previously clarified that the Pax Silica hub is not envisioned as a cluster of hyperscale data centers, but as an industrial hub that would include the manufacturing of semiconductors and microchips used in computers, laptops, electric vehicles, and other technologies. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: More than 60% of Germany’s female soldiers report harassment or abuse
articles.summary:
Defence minister says extent of sexual misconduct found by study is ‘unacceptable’, as military tries to attract more recruits

Germany’s defence minister has promised a “zero tolerance”…

blocks.text: Germany’s defence minister has promised a “zero tolerance” approach to sexual abuse in the armed forces after a study found soldiers, particularly women, faced extensive harassment within the ranks.

The first comprehensive study of its kind into the Bundeswehr, conducted by the Centre for Military History and Social Sciences in Potsdam and released this week, comes as the military is trying to attract new recruits in response to global threats.

It found that more than 60% of female soldiers had reported experiencing some form of sexual harassment or abuse while on duty, ranging from sexually explicit remarks and degrading rituals to sexual violence.

Nearly 40% of the 4,000 women who responded to the survey said they had been addressed with suggestive comments and sexualised remarks, while 15% reported being harassed with mobile phone pictures taken against their will and in some cases altered using AI.
Just over 8% reported having been physically attacked, and 2% said they had been the victims of sexual violence.
Around 19% of male ‌soldiers had experienced a similar form of sexual misconduct, with non-binary or gay soldiers disproportionately affected, the study found.

Boris Pistorius, the defence minister, said the figures were “unacceptable”, in particular for a military that is trying to considerably increase its numbers. The Bundeswehr has pumped billions into boosting both personnel and equipment. Military bosses have set a target of 260,000 active-duty troops and 200,000 reservists by 2035, in the hope of avoiding the introduction of conscription.

Pistorius said he was struck by the finding that women in units with a higher proportion of other women were less frequently affected, which he said “argues in favour of recruiting more women into the Bundeswehr”.

He said he had been advised by some colleagues to ditch the study, over fears it would sully the reputation of the military. To do so, he said, would be akin to “turning a blind eye”, which in the long term would do more damage to the Bundeswehr. The study would be repeated every year, he added.
“Zero tolerance applies to sexual harassment within the Bundeswehr,” the minister said.

Pistorius expressed concern over a high level of reluctance to report incidents. About a third of those surveyed said they did not or would not report incidents because of a lack of trust in what their superiors would do.
after newsletter promotion
Before the study results were made public, Pistorius set up a hotline this month, meant to serve military personnel, which is to be staffed around the clock, and is called HELP.

In future, Pistorius said, those who made complaints should receive more information about the status of their proceedings, after victims said they were often left in the dark, but expected to continue serving.

The ministry said that, of 45,000 active or former members of the armed forces contacted to participate in the survey, 18% responded. It said its analysis showed that the figures were nevertheless representative.

articles.title: US disrupts North Korea's $400 million crypto scam, FBI says
articles.summary: The US has seized servers linked to a North Korean scam that used fake video meetings and deepfakes to steal more than $400 million in crypto, and has moved to seize $1.2 billion that was taken from…

image.caption: Earlier, the FBI had attributed the massive Binance cryptocurrency heist to North Korea-linked hackersImage: Jenny Kane/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United States Justice Department said Thursday it had seized cloud infrastructure used by North Korean hackers in a video-call scam that has stolen more than $400 million (€361 million) in cryptocurrency over 18 months.
It also said it had court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion taken in the recent Binance hack.
What do we know?
The Federal Bureau of Investigation calls the scam "FaceStealer."

According to the Justice Department, hackers sent meeting invitations from accounts taken over from earlier victims. Once a target joins, the hackers record their webcam video and play a prerecorded clip of a previous victim the target knows, so trusted contacts appear to be present. The FBI says hackers are also starting to use AI-generated deepfakes of well-known crypto figures.
The hackers then stage a fake technical error and offer a link to "fix" it, which installs malware, the department said. In some cases, they waited months, or over a year, before stealing funds.
After that, they use the victim's contacts to find new targets.
Cryptocurrency giant Binance hit by $6.3 billion hack
Who were the targets of the scam?

Most targets work in crypto and other internet-related fields, and the hackers are increasingly going after open-source software developers, apparently to enable supply-chain attacks, the department said.
Under a federal warrant, the FBI seized more than 900 webcam videos of victims.
"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough," said Patrick Grandy, who heads the FBI's Los Angeles field office.
The FBI ties FaceStealer to a hacking cluster known as Sapphire Sleet or UNC1069. It is separate from the North Korean military hackers blamed for the Binance theft.
What happened to Binance?

In the Binance case, the FBI said the group known as TraderTraitor stole more than $6 billion (5.4 billion euros) on or around October 29. AP put the figure at about $6.3 billion (5.7 billion euros) and called it the biggest crypto heist on record. US agencies and private firms have since frozen more than $2.7 billion (2.44 billion euros), the department said.
Authorities usually file a forfeiture claim in court, after which a judge decides who has a rightful claim to the recovered funds, AP reported.

"North Korea's government bankrolls its rogue regime and illicit weapons program through cryptocurrency theft," said M. Scott Proctor, the department's principal deputy assistant attorney general for national security.
North Korea has denied involvement in the Binance hack.

articles.title: Minister’s office said contractor should handle CFMEU or lose work in Victoria, Big Build inquiry hears
articles.summary:
Royal commission also hears from construction company employee who says workers were ‘fearful’ of union

  • Get our

blocks.text: A major contractor on a troubled Victorian rail project shut down by union officials was warned that the minister’s office felt it would not “have any more work” in the state if it did not resolve the industrial dispute, a royal commission has heard.

The royal commission into the integrity of major public and civil infrastructure construction projects in Victoria heard from a Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority (Vida) official for the first time on Friday.
Vida was strongly criticised by counsel assisting the commission, Chris Young KC, on Thursday for its failure to disclose relevant evidence in a timely manner to the investigation.
The commission’s November public hearings, which are set to run until 20 November, are focusing on a 2022 level crossing removal project at Gap Road in Sunbury.

The commission previously heard that Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU) officials shut down the site because of purported safety concerns, only for them to allow it to continue after two of their own health and safety representatives were appointed, and the project changed its traffic and labour hire companies to CFMEU-aligned firms.

Peter Wilkinson, a former Vida official who is now the executive general manager of the Suburban Rail Loop authority and a civil engineer, said that at the height of an industrial dispute at Gap Road he spoke about the need for work to resume on the project with Evan Tattersall, his manager at Vida.

He said Tattersall told him on either 6 or 7 June 2022 that he had discussed the issue with the minister’s office, and Wilkinson assumed that meant the office of the then-minister for transport infrastructure, Jacinta Allan.
Tattersall told him, Wilkinson said, “that if they can’t handle the industrial [relations] in Victoria, they can’t have any more work”.
Tattersall was referring to the contractors on the site, John Holland and CPB Constructions, Wilkinson said.

Wilkinson said he was aware at the time that the contractors were tendering for the airport rail, another major state government funded infrastructure project, but that he did not know if the minister’s office also knew this.

Wilkinson said Tattersall did not tell him what he should do with the information from the minister’s office, but he passed it on to Joe Aygur, the general manager of the Rail Network Alliance involved in the project’s delivery.
Aygur told the commission about the warning on Tuesday.

When asked by Young why no record of his conversation with Tattersall existed, Wilkinson said “probably one reason is that it was moving very quickly, so it was conversation that we had to keep it moving, rather than there being a need to formally record it.”
Wilkinson was also asked about a meeting scheduled in Allan’s parliament house office for 5pm on 7 June 2022 – the day work recommenced at Gap Road.
He was listed as an optional attendee on an online invite for the meeting, but said he could not recall if he attended.

The commission also heard on Friday from Stephen Villella, who worked for CPD Constructions and was the delivery director at the site, about the meeting at the union headquarters that ultimately ended the dispute.
He said it had been “extremely galling” for construction company officials to have to “bend the knee” by meeting with the CFMEU to resolve the matter.
Villella said none of the safety concerns raised by the union were serious enough to force work to stop at the site.
Workers on the project were fearful of the CFMEU and would stay in the lunchroom for long periods once they started to attend.
“They didn’t want to come [to work] at all,” Villella said.
“They were fearful of what would happen to them organisationally and individually if they did.”

Villella said he disagreed with evidence given early in the week by a former CFMEU organiser Paul Tzimas about those on site choosing not to work, saying they were heavily pressured by union officials.
Villella said that in the meeting with the CFMEU, a union organiser Joe Myles suggested collaborating would assist in winning future tenders such as the Melbourne airport rail project.
He said Myles also suggested he had direct lines to Allan’s office.
Villella said he was not surprised by Myles’ claim about having communication to the ministers office, as he had seen what had happened to the industry over the past 10 years.
Villella said Myles left abruptly in the first half of the about 30 minute meeting, which he said felt like a snub.
But he rejected a suggestion by counsel for Myles that it was not the union official, but rather Tzimas, who raised the list of union demands for the Gap Road project.
After construction managers agreed to the demands, work on the site resumed as normal.
“Amazingly, all our safety issues ceased,” Villella said.

Chris Carr SC, senior counsel assisting the commission, said that after the rebuke issued by Young on Thursday to Vida, he was “happy to report there has been substantial production of highly relevant material overnight”.
He said that production had led to several lines of inquiry, which meant the commission was unlikely to hear from witnesses again until Tuesday.

articles.title: Sara Duterte's GenCorp declaration may be 'Freudian slip,' says lawyer
articles.summary: If the vice president wasn't a GenCorp stockholder, why did she receive P2.14 million?

blocks.text: November 13, 2026 | 12:18pm
Composite image shows defense witness Suzette Balucanag-Punay (R) during the 42nd day of the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte (L) on Nov. 11, 2026.
AFP; Senate PRIB; Philstar.com composite

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte's declaration that she was a stockholder of GenCorp Industries Inc. may have been a "Freudian slip" prompted by the P2.14 million she received from the company, lawyer Paolo Tamase said.

Tamase's observation followed testimony from Suzette Balucanag-Punay, in-house counsel for GenCorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., who told the Senate impeachment court that Duterte had no ownership stake in GenCorp despite listing herself as a stockholder in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
Punay acknowledged, however, that Duterte received more than P2 million from 2022 to 2025 in payments the defense described as a "return of capital."

In an interview one ONE News on Wednesday, November 11, Tamase distinguished between a return "of" capital, which refers to the repayment of an investor's original investment, and a return "on" capital, which refers to profits earned from that investment.

"To use, concretely, the examples from today's impeachment trial ... if the capital invested by the vice president is P48,000, then return 'of' capital would simply be giving her back the P48,000 she invested in the corporation," Tamase said.
He questioned how Duterte could have received P2.14 million if the payments were merely a return of her original investment.
Tamase described the payments as "a red flag," arguing that they raised questions about Duterte's financial interest in GenCorp despite the defense's assertion that she was not a stockholder.

"While they may have been able to explain that the vice president really was not a stockholder of GenCorp, they were able to open a new avenue that she may have business interests that were not properly declared," he said.

Alleged unexplaned wealth. The question of Duterte's financial interest in GenCorp is among the issues raised in the impeachment proceedings over her alleged unexplained wealth—the remaining impeachment article against her.
GenCorp is listed in Duterte's SALN as a company in which she holds shares, although its corporate filings do not name her as a stockholder.
The company is also alleged to have left more than P1 billion in bank inflows off its its books between 2023 and 2025.
Forensic financial analyst Alexander Cabrera, the prosecution's final witness, attributed roughly 20% of GenCorp's alleged undeclared income to Duterte, an estimate he described as "conservative."
Cabrera estimated Duterte's alleged unexplained wealth at at least P817.87 million.

His computation covered bank balances allegedly omitted from her SALN, undeclared properties, bank deposits exceeding the reported income of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, and their estimated share of undeclared income from companies they own.
Defense drops bank witnesses. The impeachment trial was adjourned Thursday, November 12, after the defense requested the cancelation of Friday's hearing.
The defense also withdrew all 16 bank officials it had previously listed as witnesses to testify about Duterte's banking records.

blocks.text: Software giant Microsoft on Thursday said it was working to fix a global outage affecting its Microsoft 365 apps, including Outlook and Teams.
Outage tracker Downdetector received reports from 74 countries and territories within about an hour.

The outage, which blocked users from accessing their e-mail and other services, also impacted Microsoft 365 connectors used by the companies OpenAI and Anthropic, which said tools were not working as expected.

Downdetector logged nearly 130,000 US reports of Outlook problems shortly after 1 p.m. EST (1800 GMT). Some customers reported having trouble sending and receiving e-mail; others said the program was entirely inaccessible.
Outages of the Teams workplace messaging app were also reported, as well as other Microsoft 365 services such as the AI assistant Copilot.

Microsoft initially said on X that it was aware that users were "experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas," noting that part of its infrastructure was "experiencing elevated load" that was "likely contributing to connectivity errors."
"We are aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.

Microsoft said some restarted servers stopped responding again once traffic returned. In an update at 0254 GMT Friday, the company said its latest changes had not worked as expected and it was looking for other ways to restore service.

articles.title: Makati court issues extradition warrant on Quiboloy, co-accused in U.S. charges
articles.summary: Makati court finds probable cause, also issues hold departure orders against 3.

blocks.text: November 13, 2026 | 11:50am

Apollo Quiboloy, head of "the Kingdom of Jesus Christ," a non-Catholic religious group and spiritual adviser of president-elect Rodrigo Duterte, speaks during a press conference in Davao City in southern island of Mindanao on May 23, 2016.
AFP / Manman Dejeto

MANILA, Philippines — A Makati court has issued extradition warrants against religious leader Apollo Quiboloy and two co-accused following a request from the United States, the Department of Justice said.

The Makati Regional Trial Court Branch 145 issued the warrants on Thursday, November 12 against Quiboloy, Teresita Tolibas Dandan and Helen Panilag after finding probable cause, according to the DOJ. Quiboloy, however, is already detained.

"On 12 November 2026, pursuant to Section 4, Rule 2 of the Rules on Extradition Proceedings, the court issued an Extradition Warrant of Arrest against the foregoing individuals, after finding probable cause that: (a) each extraditee is the person named in the corresponding foreign arrest warrant and indictment, (b) that the offenses charged are extraditable offenses, and (c) that each extraditee committed the offense or offenses charged," the DOJ said.
The court also issued hold departure orders against the three "to prevent any attempt by each of them to depart from the Philippines."
What happens next?

Under the Rules on Extradition Proceedings, the court must personally serve the extraditee with a summons and copies of the petition and its annexes once it receives notice that an arrest has been carried out.
The extraditee then has 15 days from receipt to file a verified answer.
Philstar.com has sought clarification from the DOJ on how Quiboloy and his two co-accused would be brought under the jurisdiction of the Makati court, but the department has yet to respond.
The DOJ earlier said the US extradition request had reached the Makati RTC on November 9.
US criminal allegations
The US case against Quiboloy includes allegations involving international human trafficking, sex trafficking, conspiracy and bulk cash smuggling.
A US federal grand jury indicted Quiboloy in 2021 on charges that include conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion, and sex trafficking of children.
US prosecutors have accused Quiboloy and other members of his Kingdom of Jesus Christ organization of recruiting women and girls as personal assistants and coercing them into sex.
In the Philippines, Quiboloy remains detained while facing child and sexual abuse cases before a Quezon City court and a qualified human trafficking case before a Pasig court.
Quiboloy denies all allegations against him.

The Sandiganbayan Third Division acquitted former Albay governor Edcel Greco "Grex" Lagman on indirect bribery and violation of Anti-Illegal Numbers Game law due to insufficient evidence.

items: Toyota Fortuner allegedly being used to deliver the jueteng payola to Lagman

blocks.text: "Pursuant to the Rules on Evidence and related jurisprudence, the truth of the matters contained in these independently relevant statements cannot now be used to give context or assign corroborative roles to these remaining pieces of evidence, thereby, leaving the Court with no inference to be derived in determining whether Lagman is indeed guilty of the crimes charged," the Sandiganbayan said.

articles.title: ASEAN leaders to agree on new energy measures as Middle East crisis drags on
articles.summary: Southeast Asian leaders are expected to agree on new measures to deal with the energy crunch from the Middle East conflict when they meet in Manila next week, the spokesperson of the Philippines'…

blocks.text: November 13, 2026 | 11:08am
Flags of the ASEAN member states line the grounds of the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay on Nov. 12, 2026, as the Philippines prepares to host the upcoming regional summit.
The Philippine STAR / Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders are expected to agree on new measures to deal with the energy crunch from the Middle East conflict when they meet in Manila next week, the spokesperson of the Philippines' ASEAN chairship said Friday, November 13.

Asked how the government would measure the success of the Philippines' year as ASEAN chair, spokesperson Dominic Xavier Imperial acknowledged the region was "still feeling the impacts of the Middle East crisis."

In response, the region's leaders are expected to take "additional measures and decisions" on the energy situation, among other issues, when they meet next week, Imperial told reporters at a briefing.
Food security, the fight against transnational crime and online scams, and greater protection for migrant workers, particularly Filipinos, are also on the agenda, Imperial said.
The 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, chaired by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., will run from Sunday, November 15, to Tuesday, November 17.

The Philippines relies heavily on imported oil and has been reeling from high fuel prices since the conflict between Iran and US-Israeli forces broke out in February this year and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Prices have eased in recent weeks following greater expectations of a de-escalation in the war after the Democratic Party's sweep of the US midterm elections.

The Department of Energy announced a sharp gasoline rollback of P16.80 per liter for November 10 to 16 on hopes of a diplomatic settlement in the conflict, though local prices remain well above prewar levels.

At their first summit of the year, in Cebu in May, ASEAN leaders adopted a proposal for a regional oil stockpiling mechanism and agreed to speed up ratification of a regional petroleum security pact, while voicing serious concern over the conflict's impact on the region's economies and energy routes.
Imperial said the study on the stockpile was still being done, and the Philippines hoped its results would feed into the Manila summit. As a result, the size of the possible reserve has not been set.

On the updated ASEAN Petroleum Security Agreement, under which members would supply fuel to neighbors facing severe shortages, Imperial said the bloc's members were still working through its ratification.
The number of ASEAN members that have ratified the agreement so far is "four or five," Imperial said.
This includes the Philippines, as Marcos previously confirmed the country's ratification of the deal in his State of the Nation Address in July.
The bloc has been hoping for a full ratification by this month's summit, which is also the last high-level engagement during Manila's term as ASEAN chair.
Signed in October 2025, the updated agreement will replace a 2009 agreement and take effect 90 days after ratification is formally deposited with the ASEAN secretary-general.

articles.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
articles.summary: More than 900 victims are thought to have fallen prey to the FaceStealer scheme in the last 18 months.

blocks.text: State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.
More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.

"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.
This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company.
US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.

Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.

According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.
Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction.

A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.
Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.
The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".

"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.
"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

articles.title: Maryland's Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for U.S. Senate leadership post
articles.summary: Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate majority leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party…

image.caption: U.S. Sen. Chris Van Hollen says he'll will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer. (Jose Luis Magana/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Updated

Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate majority leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections.
Van Hollen says Democrats 'need new leadership'
Van Hollen said in a statement that "the American people called for change" and that is why he is running.

"It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," Van Hollen said. "This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate Majority Leader."

Van Hollen's challenge comes after he said he was considering a bid and after Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December.
U.S. Sen. Chuck Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win. (Mariam Zuhaib/The Associated Press)
The race will be the first contested election for Democratic leader in decades.

The question of whether to re-elect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators will not say publicly how they will vote. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election, and Schumer recruited many of the party's winning candidates and raised money for them.
'I'm going to win it': Schumer
Schumer has been talking to Democratic senators since the election about forming an agenda for 2027.
"I'm going to win it," Schumer told The Associated Press in an interview last week.
In a statement after Van Hollen's announcement, Schumer said he welcomes any discussion about the future of the caucus.

"I'm proud of what we've accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader," Schumer said. "I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people."

While Schumer is the favourite to win, Van Hollen's run exposes a rift in the party that has put Schumer on the defensive since he sided with Republicans on a spending vote in March 2025. Even as he has redeemed himself within his caucus since then — leading them through a government shutdown last year and orchestrating huge wins in the election — many in the Democratic base are agitating for generational change.
Van Hollen, 67, is not that much younger than Schumer, 75. But he has positioned himself as a new face in the party. He has also said he is considering a run for president.
El-Sayed backs Van Hollen

While most Democratic senators have either said they are supporting Schumer or are undecided, Van Hollen has at least one backer in next year's caucus: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who won a competitive election in his state last week, posted on X Thursday night that their majority will need "bold leadership."
U.S. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed is backing Van Hollen to be the Democrats' leader in the U.S. Senate. (Kylie Cooper/Reuters)

"I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience," El-Sayed wrote. "We need both right now. Which is why I'm proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority."
Several senators have said they are backing Schumer, including incoming Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown, who beat Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week.

Maine Sen. Angus King, an Independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the election, issued a statement after Van Hollen's announcement: "Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?
"Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible," King wrote.

articles.title: Darth Vader strikes back at auction as his lightsaber from two original Star Wars films reclaims the record from Luke Skywalker's prop
articles.summary: Darth Vader's lightsaber sold for nearly $5 million, breaking the record set by Luke Skywalker's in July. The hilt, made from a 1950s camera flash attachment, was used in two of the original…

image.caption: The hilt was made from a 1950s camera flash attachment and reinforced to hold wooden blades for fight scenes (FILE: 06/08/2025)Image: Joanna Chan/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A lightsaber prop made for "Star Wars" villain Darth Vader sold for $4.875 million (€4.4 million) on Thursday, setting an auction record for a collectible from the franchise, according to Dallas-based Heritage Auctions.
The iconic prop was used in two defining duels between Darth Vader and Luke Skywalker in the original "Star Wars" trilogy.
Which scenes featured Vader's lightsaber?

Vader wielded the lightsaber in the climactic Cloud City duel in "The Empire Strikes Back" (1980), where he cuts off Luke's hand. When Luke accuses him of killing his father, Vader replies with one of the saga's most famous lines: "No. I am your father."
The same lightsaber returned for their final duel in "Return of the Jedi" (1983). This time, Luke cuts off Vader's hand but refuses to kill him.

Vader's lightsaber set an auction record for a screen-used "Star Wars" prop in 2025. Luke's lightsaber from the same Cloud City duel broke it in July. In the latest twist, Vader struck back to reclaim the record.

blocks.caption: Luke and Vader's first lightsaber duel took place in Cloud City, a long time ago in a galaxy far, far away (FILE: 1980)Image: 20th Century Fox/Everett Collection/picture alliance

blocks.text: Actor David Prowse and stunt performer Bob Anderson both wielded the saber as Darth Vader. It may also have been used in the original 1977 "Star Wars" film, but the auctioneers could not confirm that.
What inspired the lightsaber?

"Star Wars" creator George Lucas drew on Errol Flynn swashbucklers and the legends of King Arthur. He imagined the Jedi as peacekeepers guided by chivalry and honor and wanted a weapon that suited that role.

In the original "Star Wars," Luke's Jedi mentor, Obi-Wan Kenobi, gives him his father's lightsaber, describing it as "not as clumsy or random as a blaster" and calling it "an elegant weapon for a more civilized age."

Lucas first imagined the Jedi carrying ordinary swords. He gave them futuristic blades that could deflect blaster fire. As he put it in the Lucasfilm featurette "The Birth of the Lightsaber": "A laser sword in a world of ray guns would be a perfect defensive weapon."
How was Vader's lightsaber made and identified?

The hilt began life as a 1950s British camera flash attachment. Prop makers added black plastic grips and tiny magnifying lenses from a calculator display. Heritage described it as "built to perform rather than merely to be seen." The crew reinforced the hilt to hold interchangeable wooden blades and screwed the grips into place after they came loose during fight scenes.

blocks.caption: More than four decades after "The Empire Strikes Back," Luke and Vader's rivalry remains iconic, even inspiring a drone show over Seoul (FILE: 05/05/2026)Image: Kichul Shin/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: For "The Empire Strikes Back," the crew initially covered the wooden blades in reflective material and later painted them white. After filming, the effects team used the rods as a guide, tracing their movements frame by frame to create the blazing red blade seen on screen.
Heritage matched a distinctive bend in the hilt's belt ring to a production photo from "The Empire Strikes Back" and a dent at its base to a close-up in "Return of the Jedi."

articles.title: Sara Duterte's defense drops all 16 bank witnesses in trial
articles.summary: All 16 bank officials initially lined up as Sara Duterte defense witnesses are now off the list.

blocks.text: November 13, 2026 | 10:18am
Defense counsel Michael Poa speaks before the Senate impeachment court during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Nov. 12, 2026.
Senate of the Philippines via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte has dropped 16 bank officials from its witness list in her impeachment trial, including a Bank of the Philippine Islands executive whom prosecutors wanted to question about her alleged dollar accounts.

The latest witness withdrawn was BPI senior vice president Paul Roderick Ysmael, who was supposed to authenticate a letter concerning the bank accounts of Duterte and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte.

Defense counsel Michael Poa said Ysmael was no longer needed since he had already admitted writing the letter during an earlier court proceeding. The document had also been marked as evidence for the defense.
“It would be in the interest of time that we just dispensed with this witness,” Poa told the Senate impeachment court on Thursday, November 12.
The defense had dropped 15 other bank officials from its witness list a day earlier.
Prosecutors, however, said they wanted to question Ysmael about BPI records indicating that Duterte maintained dollar accounts.
“Unfortunately, before we had a chance to cross-examine the witness about this dollar account, they dispensed with the testimony,” prosecution counsel Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said.

Private prosecutor James Bryan Ibrahim Alih also sought permission to make additional manifestations on the documents subpoenaed for Ysmael's testimony, but presiding officer Chiz Escudero denied the request, saying that the prosecution had already rested its case.

The BPI accounts resurfaced in October when Anti-Money Laundering Council Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified that Duterte and her father maintained a joint account at the bank's Julia Vargas branch in Pasig City. A covered transaction report showed that P9.1 million was withdrawn from the account in a single transaction in April 2013.
Meanwhile, prosecutors said the defense had yet to directly challenge the P817 million in alleged unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte by financial forensic expert Alexander Cabrera.
By the end of the 43rd day of proceedings on Thursday, the defense had presented six witnesses over four hearing days but had yet to directly rebut Cabrera's computation.

articles.title: Chris Van Hollen to challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
articles.summary:
Maryland Democrat challenges party leader after midterms sweep, saying: ‘The American people called for change’

Chris Van Hollen, the Democratic senator of Maryland, said Thursday that he…

blocks.text: Chris Van Hollen, the Democratic senator of Maryland, announced on Thursday that he is challenging Chuck Schumer for the role of Senate majority leader when Democrats regain the chamber’s majority in January.

“In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies – but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said in a statement posted on social media.

“It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”

Schumer, the leader of the Democratic minority in the current Senate, responded less than a minute later in a social media post of his own. “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead,” Schumer wrote. “I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together – 55 seats and counting is an amazing result – and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.”
The battle pits a progressive Democrat, Van Hollen, against a centrist, Schumer.
Van Hollen’s challenge comes after he said he was considering a bid and after Schumer said he had the necessary support to win. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December.

The race will be the first contested election for Democratic leader in decades. The question of whether to re-elect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators will not say publicly how they will vote. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election, and Schumer recruited many of the party’s winning candidates and raised money for them. But some of the winning candidates, most notably Michigan’s senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, did not initially have Schumer’s support.
Schumer has been talking to Democratic senators since the election about forming an agenda for 2027.
“I’m going to win it,” Schumer told the Associated Press in an interview last week.

articles.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president says it makes sense for European leaders to be involved as Ukraine hopes to eventually join the EU.

blocks.text: Ukraine's president has welcomed a pledge from US envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, to include delegates from the European Union in the next round of peace talks with Russia.
European leaders have expressed deepening security concerns this week, and Volodymyr Zelensky said bringing them into the talks would ensure the EU has a "voice" in negotiations.

Kushner and Witkoff met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday evening as part of a busy day of shuttle diplomacy - they met Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier, who said that Russia's position on the war - and its demand for territory - has not changed.
The meetings follow talks in Abu Dhabi last week that failed to reach a breakthrough in ending the war.
But Thursday did see Russia and Ukraine agree to another prisoner exchange - the largest swap yet since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.
Kushner said it would return "thousands of people to their families", but further details like how many prisoners would be exchanged or a timeline, were not given.
Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union.
On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important."
He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table".
"He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added.
Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.
Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.

Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player".
Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) Micheál Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war.

"Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters.
Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common.
Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky.

Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

blocks.text: Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said.
After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement.
Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August.
The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking.

Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are reportedly looking into civil action.
"Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday.
A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police.
Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me".
"To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued.
